_about: Episode 2 outline, beat level.  The Fountain script (ep2/script.fountain) is written from it; each beat is a [[beat: id]] note there.
'gist' is a sketch of what is said, not final dialogue.  'lines' lists the script's stable line IDs.
Every number here is claimed against math_objects.json; run check_outline.py after any change.
title: The Geometry of a Kitten

scenes._comment: Series main title, then this episode's subtitle; see titles/outline.json.
scenes.subtitle: sub.ep2

scenes.title: Special how?
scenes.summary: Quick replay of Episode 1's line-up of losing hands. Sophie decides she needs a picture.

beats.purpose: Replay Episode 1's line-up of losing hands; Sophie decides she needs a picture
beats.gist: SOPHIE: These hands lost; forty-five we only tested. Special how? PASCAL: They lost. SOPHIE: Losers with a secret. I need a picture.

scenes.title: Seven points
scenes.summary: The Fano plane: seven points and seven lines, the circle included. Pick 1 and 4 and their line supplies 2; pick 4 and 5 and the circle supplies 6. Pascal objects that a circle can't be a line; Sophie: it obeys the rule.

beats.purpose: Sophie draws the Fano plane: a finite geometry of seven points and seven lines
beats.gist: SOPHIE: A tiny geometry, the Fano plane: seven points, seven lines. ADA: Only seven? SOPHIE: A finite geometry.

beats.purpose: Any two points lie on exactly one line: 1 and 4 call up 2
beats.gist: SOPHIE: Any two points, exactly one line. Pick one and four. (Pause.) Their line calls up two.

beats.purpose: 4 and 5 call up 6 along the circle; Pascal objects that a circle can't be a line
beats.gist: SOPHIE: Four and five: the circle brings six. PASCAL: A circle isn't a line. SOPHIE: It obeys the rule. EULER: A line is whatever obeys the rules.

scenes.title: Twelve points, five at a time
scenes.summary: Read S(2,3,7) aloud, then ask for S(5,6,12): every five of twelve points in exactly one six-point block. Count: 792 five-sets, six in each block, so 132 blocks. Name them hexads. Ada: if such a thing exists.

beats.purpose: The Fano plane read aloud as a Steiner system S(2,3,7)
beats.gist: SOPHIE: Every two of seven points on exactly one line of three: a Steiner system, S(2,3,7).

beats.purpose: Sophie asks for S(5,6,12): twelve points, every five in exactly one block of six
beats.gist: SOPHIE: Twelve points, blocks of six, every five in exactly one block. EULER: The small Witt design. ADA: How many blocks?

beats.purpose: Counting settles the size: 792 five-sets, six in each block, so 132 blocks
establishes: If S(5,6,12) exists, it has 132 blocks
beats.gist: SOPHIE: Seven hundred ninety-two fives; six in a block; so a hundred thirty-two blocks.

beats.purpose: The blocks are named hexads; Ada doubts that such a design exists

conjectures.text: Does a design S(5,6,12) actually exist?

beats.gist: SOPHIE: We'll call each block a hexad. ADA: If such a thing exists.

scenes.title: Two moves on a ring
scenes.summary: Twelve labels on a ring: 0 to 10 mod 11, plus infinity. Seed Q = 0 and the five nonzero squares. Two moves, add one and negative reciprocal, keep making new six-sets until the orbit closes at 132. Delete each point from each block: 792 distinct five-sets, each once. The design exists.

beats.purpose: Euler makes the twelve points a clock mod 11 plus infinity: the projective line
beats.gist: EULER: Zero to ten around a clock, infinity in the middle. Ten plus one is zero: mod eleven. The projective line.

beats.purpose: The seed: zero and the five nonzero squares mod 11
beats.gist: EULER: Zero and the nonzero squares: one, four, nine, five, three. SOPHIE: Our first hexad?

beats.purpose: Two moves permute the ring: add one, and the negative reciprocal
beats.gist: EULER: Move one: add one; infinity stays put. Move two: negative reciprocal; zero and infinity trade places. Each is a permutation.

beats.purpose: Both moves applied again and again: the orbit closes at exactly 132
beats.gist: EULER: Apply both moves to every new set. SOPHIE: It stopped. EULER: A hundred thirty-two: the orbit of the seed.

beats.purpose: Every five-set appears exactly once among the 132; five points call up their sixth. The design exists
establishes: The orbit of Q is a Steiner system S(5,6,12)
beats.gist: EULER: Seven hundred ninety-two fives, each exactly once. SOPHIE: One, two, three, four, five... EULER: ...call up seven. ADA: It exists.

scenes.title: Curtis's kitten
scenes.summary: The triangular kitten: corners infinity, 0, 1, and repeated labels that name the same point. At each corner the nine other points form a 3 x 3 affine plane; rows, columns and two wrapped diagonal directions are lines. Shown, not named: the wrap is arithmetic mod 3 (named in Episode 3). A row plus a column is a cross; the four points left are a square.

beats.purpose: The same twelve points as Curtis's triangular kitten, corners infinity, 0 and 1
beats.gist: SOPHIE: Another picture of the same twelve points: Curtis's kitten. PASCAL: It's a triangle. SOPHIE: With three corners: infinity, zero and one.

beats.purpose: Repeated labels name the same point
beats.gist: SOPHIE: Three sixes, but one point.

beats.purpose: At each corner the other nine points form a 3 x 3 affine plane
beats.gist: SOPHIE: Seen from each corner, the other nine points make a three-by-three grid: an affine plane.

beats.purpose: Rows, columns and diagonals are lines, and a diagonal wraps around (mod 3, shown but not named)
beats.gist: SOPHIE: Rows are lines, so are columns, and diagonals. This one runs off the edge and comes back. EULER: Like a clock with three hours.

beats.purpose: A row plus a column is a cross; the four points left over are a square
beats.gist: SOPHIE: A row plus a column makes a cross. The four left over make a square.

scenes.title: Four families
scenes.summary: A line plus the three corners; two parallel lines; a cross plus its own corner; a square plus the other two corners. 12 + 12 + 54 + 54 = 132, exactly the orbit from the ring. Two pictures, one object.

beats.purpose: Family 1: a line plus the three corners, twelve hexads
beats.gist: SOPHIE: One: a line, plus all three corners. Twelve.

beats.purpose: Family 2: two parallel lines, twelve hexads
beats.gist: SOPHIE: Two: a pair of parallel lines. Twelve more.

beats.purpose: Family 3: a cross plus its own corner, 3 x 18 = 54 hexads
beats.gist: SOPHIE: Three: a cross, plus its own corner. Fifty-four.

beats.purpose: Family 4: a square plus the other two corners, 54 hexads
beats.gist: SOPHIE: Four: a square, plus the other two corners. Fifty-four again.

beats.purpose: 12 + 12 + 54 + 54 = 132, exactly the ring's orbit: two pictures, one object
establishes: The four kitten families are exactly the 132 hexads of the ring
beats.gist: ADA: Twelve, twelve, fifty-four, fifty-four: a hundred thirty-two. The same as Euler's ring. SOPHIE: Two pictures, one object.

scenes.title: Back to the cards
scenes.summary: Relabel the points as card values (the shuffle labeling). Episode 1's losing hands light up as hexads: 1 to 6, the 24-hand, the end of the worked game, and the 45-hand too. Euler's guess holds: the 28 Pascal left Ada is a hexad. Why hexads lose is still open.

beats.purpose: Relabel the points as card values: the shuffle labeling
beats.gist: SOPHIE: Give every point a card value. Infinity becomes zero, zero becomes six. The shuffle labeling.

beats.purpose: 1 to 6 is a square plus two corners; its complement, the 45-hand, is the cross in the same grid plus the third corner
beats.gist: SOPHIE: One to six: a square plus corners one and six. EULER: And forty-five is the cross in the same grid, plus corner zero.

beats.purpose: Ada's 24 and the end of the worked game are hexads too
beats.gist: SOPHIE: Ada's twenty-four is a hexad, and so is the end of our first game. ADA: Every hand that lost is a hexad.

beats.purpose: Euler's guess holds: the 28 Pascal left Ada is a hexad
beats.gist: EULER: And the twenty-eight? SOPHIE: A hexad too. EULER: I guessed right. PASCAL: I knew it all along.

beats.purpose: The special hands are hexads; why hexads lose is still open
beats.gist: SOPHIE: The special hands are hexads. But why do hexads lose? I can't see that yet.

scenes.title: No memorizing
scenes.summary: PASCAL: Great. We memorize all 132 and I never lose. ADA: Absolutely not.

beats.purpose: Pascal wants to memorize all 132; Ada refuses
beats.gist: PASCAL: We memorize all 132 and I never lose. ADA: Absolutely not. PASCAL: Just the first fifty? ADA: There's a better way.

scenes._comment: End-credits screenplay (end_credits/outline.json), then the next_time tail.
